root_idea.summary: The root centrally expresses turning aside or away: a movement toward one side that can extend to diverting another from a course.
root_idea.development: From this orientation arise meanings of avoidance, prevention, lateral position, facing or proximity, and directed attention. Separate lexical branches include clamour or laughter and the blood-mixed purulent fluid called صَدِيد.

senses.definition: To turn away from, avoid, shun, or be averse to something or someone.
senses.usage_conditions: Intransitive or used with عَنْ; includes turning the face away and refusing or abstaining from the object.

senses.definition: To turn someone away or back; to divert, prevent, or hinder someone from doing something or reaching a course.
senses.usage_conditions: Transitive construction with عَنْ; the object may be a person, an action, or a path. Passive usage means to be turned away or hindered.

senses.definition: To cry out, vociferate, or raise a clamour.
senses.usage_conditions: A distinct vocalization is reported for صَدَّ يَصِدُّ; the Quranic occurrence at 43:57 has this lexical possibility alongside the laughter interpretation.

senses.definition: To laugh violently, loudly, or immoderately.
senses.usage_conditions: A distinct lexical use reported for the same present-tense vocalization; the supplied contextual rendering of 43:57 reflects this interpretation.

senses.definition: To cause someone to be turned away or hindered; in the passive, to be turned away or hindered.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quranic occurrence is passive. The derived Form II headword is connected lexically with the Form I turning-away and prevention construction.

senses.definition: To clap the hands or raise a clamour.
senses.usage_conditions: Attested in the Quranic derived-noun construction تَصْدِيَةً; this Quranic construction is distinct from the supplied passive occurrence at 13:33.

senses.definition: Purulent, blood-mixed fluid or ichor from a wound; in the Quran, the foul fluid offered as a drink to the inmates of Hell.
senses.usage_conditions: An adjective used substantively in the Quranic expression ماءٍ صَدِيدٍ; the fluid is described as watery pus or matter mixed with blood.

senses.definition: Hindering or preventing people from a way, especially from the path of God.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic verbal noun in constructions such as صَدٌّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ; it denotes active diversion or obstruction rather than merely personal aversion.

senses.definition: Turning away from something; aversion or abstention.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic verbal noun describes a person's refusal or turning away from an addressed matter or person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat someone with aversion and opposition.
Of a wound: to contain or generate pus, or to run with purulent matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized verbal use concerning a wound and the fluid called صَدِيد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To address or apply oneself to someone or something; to direct one's attention toward it, approach it, or seek a requested benefit from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived reflexive or middle construction; it can describe directing oneself toward an affair or person, petitioning, or seeking proximity and favor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cover oneself with a veil or covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied evidence records the feminine inflected form; the action itself is not restricted to a particular object class in the definition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The beating of a sieve by hand.
A hundred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a Persian word apparently used by Arabs; it is a loanword rather than a central Arabic derivation of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The face or front surface of the hand.
A side, flank, or lateral part: specifically the side of a valley, ravine, mountain, or road, and the edge of an arrow-notch.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The spatial sense extends to an adjacent tract, quarter, or side; the arrow usage refers to the two edges of the notch between which the bowstring rests.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal use from the more specific sense of a side or flank.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A high-rising cloud or mass of clouds appearing like a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is reported alongside سَدٌّ or سُدٌّ in this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vicinity or a near place; the place or direction in front of, opposite, or facing something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in locative expressions for being near, opposite, before, or directed toward an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An impediment or obstacle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in an idiomatic expression denying that an impediment stands in the way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The matter or affair to which one's attention is directed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the phrase بِصَدَدِ to indicate that one is addressing, considering, or returning to a subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman's veil or covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical item is a covering or screen; the source specifically records its use as a woman's garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of garment for women or young girls.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized garment term with variant identification in the transmitted lexicon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Molten silver or the material melted from silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension based on resemblance to purulent fluid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A variety of fig, white outside, black within, and very sweet.
A road or route to water.
A small animal identified variously as a serpent, lizard or gecko, or a small field animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted identifications vary; the lexical branch denotes a small reptile or similar small creature rather than one securely fixed species.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who turns away, avoids, shuns, or leaves; one who is averse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active-participle noun or adjective derived from the intransitive turning-away sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Turned away or prevented from attaining something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence illustrates the expression with being prevented from good or prosperity; that illustration is not a restriction on the object.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Cross-reference to the Form I turning-away and prevention entry; this lexical content is covered by the Form II hinder sense.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the main Form I entry.
Derivational cross-reference stating the verbal-noun relation without adding a meaning.

cautions: The occurrence at 43:57 is supplied with the contextual gloss “laughed aloud,” while the lexical evidence also records cry or clamour for the same vocalization; both materially distinct readings are retained without treating the contextual gloss as the sole lexical definition.

The Quranic Form II clapping evidence concerns the derived noun تَصْدِيَةً in the cited Quranic expression, whereas the supplied QAC Form II occurrence is the passive verb at 13:33; no unsupplied verse location is used as an example.
A historical citation attached to the صَدِيد discussion is not converted into a modern surah:ayah location; the displayed Quran example uses only the independently supplied QAC location 14:16.
The derived Form V material تَصَدَّى is retained as a broader Classical Arabic entry because no corresponding QAC Form V group is supplied.
